lineage.basis: Independently review the compiler-input source and exact ABI already bound to each target in retainedEvidence; retain each chain-specific artifact, chain ID, receipt, constructor, metadata and compiler binding. No ABI/source is borrowed from another deployment even when content hashes coincide.
lineage.historicalDecisionSuperseded: Only the prior multicall(bytes[]) exclusion for these six exact targets is superseded by newly reviewed concrete exact-eight-child scopes. Earlier source records remain unchanged as historical evidence; every other prior decision and every existing execution scope/allowedChildren list remains unchanged.
lineage.artifactRetention: Full original deployment artifact bytes, creation/deployed bytecode, metadata, compiler input and source snapshots remain content-addressed under retainedEvidence#/sourcePool/<sha256>. This record retains the complete per-target ABI/binding evidence and the reviewed execution-source bodies without duplicating artifact/bytecode payloads.

identityHashMethod.algorithm: Keccak-256 of recursively key-sorted JSON for [fn.abi], preserving array order and the actual fresh-catalog ABI fragment including internalType and names. Computed by importing and calling the repository function, not SHA-256.
identityHashMethod.childResolution: Resolve each canonical signature against the fresh active catalog contract at the same chainId and lowercase-equivalent exact address; bind its actual capabilityId and functionAbiHash. All eight children are standalone, active contract_call capabilities with no executionScope.

executionRestrictions.shape: Root must be exactly payable multicall(bytes[]) returns(bytes[]). Scope binds exactly eight distinct child IDs/signatures/ABI hashes at this SAME chain/address; no arbitrary target, selector-only, cross-chain or sibling-manager authorization.
executionRestrictions.bounds: Existing preflight rejects empty arrays and malformed offsets, overlapping elements, payloads shorter than a selector or longer than 65,536 bytes. Existing MAX_DEFI_EXECUTION_NODES=10 counts root plus children across the request: a lone root can have at most nine child calls, not ten. The eight allowed signatures define a vocabulary, not a requirement to invoke each once; duplicate authorized operations remain possible within the unchanged bound.
executionRestrictions.canonical: Outer and every nested call must decode and re-encode to identical canonical calldata; trailing bytes, selector-only invalid parameters and unknown/short child selectors remain rejected. Children must be active contract_call, match exact ID/signature/ABI hash, have no executionScope, and resolve at the root target.
executionRestrictions.excludedNestedSurfaces: Recursive multicall, createAndInitializePoolIfNecessary, all NFT transfer overloads, approve/setApprovalForAll, NFT/ERC20 permit and selfPermit variants, callbacks, getters, fallback/receive, arbitrary executors and every other method remain outside the closed child set. In particular the already standalone create-pool, transferFrom and fixed-empty-data safeTransferFrom capabilities do NOT become children.
executionRestrictions.native: Root native value must satisfy the existing nonnegative uint256 checks. The SAME outer value is passed to child canonical/native validation, mirroring delegatecall msg.value inheritance, not a separate child transfer, budget or sum. All eight actual child ABIs are payable. This admission adds no child-value override, separate funding, refund guarantee or msg.value-based per-child accounting.
executionRestrictions.grantsAndPauses: Catalog metadata supplies no grant. Custom mode must independently grant the exact root and every actually invoked child ID; root-only and child-only grants cannot authorize the other. All mode remains dynamic only for active unpaused capabilities. Global, chain, exact-contract and individual root/child capability pauses remain independently checked at preflight and final acceptance.
executionRestrictions.finalAcceptance: Keep request commitment, reviewed manifest/hash/ABI/scope identity, exact execution-plan recomputation and equality, current API-key user/wallet ownership, mode/membership, revocation/freeze/expiry and canSendTransaction checks under the existing caller-owned READ COMMITTED transaction and shared pause/key locks. Recheck grants and pauses for root and every expanded child; signing/execution boundaries and independent safety policies are unchanged.
executionRestrictions.financialNonGuarantees: This existing scope does NOT impose owner-only recipient constraints, automatically insert settlement/refund calls, prove no residual custody, impose new slippage/deadline bounds or attest pool/token balances. Those are not implied by source admission or the stronger unrelated Universal Router/V4 languages.

sourceReview.entrypoint: Inherited public payable Multicall.multicall(bytes[] calldata data) returns(bytes[] memory results). NonfungiblePositionManager inherits Multicall and declares no override; constructor binds a direct manager, not a proxy, SwapRouter or RouteProcessor.
sourceReview.target: For each array element the sole low-level dispatch is address(this).delegatecall(data[i]); neither an address argument nor any other caller-selected outer dispatch target exists. Ordinary child pool/token/wrapped-native interactions still execute their separately reviewed source semantics; self-only dispatch does not mean those external interactions disappear.
sourceReview.sender: Self delegatecall keeps the original external msg.sender and manager address/storage. NFT authorization in decreaseLiquidity/collect/burn therefore consumes the original caller's existing owner/operator authority; addLiquidity encodes that original caller as payer, not the manager. No sender substitution or appended forwarder suffix is present.
sourceReview.value: Delegatecall preserves the original msg.value for every child but does not fund the manager again. Actual available native balance changes as children spend/refund; payment uses constructor-bound WETH9 and current address(this).balance, wrapping only what is needed or pulling payer ERC20 allowance. IMulticall explicitly says msg.value should not be trusted for callable methods. Repeated child calls do not multiply deposited native currency.
sourceReview.orderingAndResults: Elements execute sequentially; successful bytes return data is stored at the matching results index. No allowFailure/partial-success flag exists.
sourceReview.revertPropagation: Every unsuccessful delegatecall aborts the whole outer transaction, rolling back prior child effects. Source reverts empty when return data is shorter than 68 bytes; otherwise advances result by four bytes and reverts with abi.decode(result,(string)). This is legacy Error(string)-style decoding, NOT byte-for-byte arbitrary revert-data bubbling; malformed/non-string error data may itself revert.
sourceReview.publicCustody: refundETH sends the ENTIRE current manager native balance to original msg.sender. unwrapWETH9 unwraps the ENTIRE current constructor-bound WETH9 balance to explicit recipient; sweepToken transfers the ENTIRE selected-token balance to explicit recipient. amountMinimum is a lower bound, not a cap. These helpers do not check NFT ownership/depositor attribution. collect recipient zero routes to manager custody. Unsettled manager balances are publicly recoverable and must never be treated as private escrow.
sourceReview.financialSemantics: decreaseLiquidity only credits owed tokens; collect performs payout with caps and rounding caveats. mint funds an initialized pool and _mints the NFT to explicit recipient without receiver callback; increaseLiquidity is permissionless caller-funded top-up benefiting its current NFT owner. No direct callback child is admitted although validated pool mint callbacks occur inside mint/increase. Existing token allowances, balances, deadlines, minimums, ticks, fee, recipient and NFT authority remain caller responsibilities.
sourceReview.settlementResponsibility: A caller wanting atomic custody cleanup must explicitly include suitable independently granted refund/unwrap/sweep children and intended recipients within the node limit. The existing scope does not mandate their presence/order or prove a full drain; source success is not a financial-safety or execution guarantee.

sourceReview.revertPropagation: Every unsuccessful delegatecall aborts the whole outer transaction, rolling back prior child effects.
